subject: Availability disruption for model-x3b: customer briefing & postmortem follow-up
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@kensington-analytics.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: support@kensington-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 27 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected 5xx spike from model-x3b affecting inference jobs

Hi Hannah,

We started seeing a sudden increase in 5xx responses and timeouts from requests routed to model-x3b around 08:50 PST this morning. It’s impacting our batch scoring pipeline (jobs that normally complete in ~12m are now timing out after retries). Error logs show repeated 503/504 and occasional 502.

We’re running on your hosted API with route pinned to x3b-v1 for the last three weeks (account KD-9412). Can you confirm whether this is a regional issue or a model-level degradation? We’ve raised an internal pager but wanted to check with you directly since this is affecting a scheduled customer run.

Marta
Director, Data Product
Kensington Analytics

Attachments: error_snippets.log (text), job-manifest-0227.json (attachment)
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@kensington-analytics.com>, support@kensington-analytics.com
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 27 Feb 2028 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 5xx spike from model-x3b affecting inference jobs

Hi Marta — thanks for the quick heads up and the logs. We are seeing elevated 5xx error rates in the us-west-2 pool specifically for model-x3b (v1) beginning ~08:40 PST. My team has opened INF-4821 and we’ve started a prioritized trie-level rollback to x3b-stable-202801 as a mitigation.

Immediate items:
- We’ve routed new requests to the stable variant for KD-9412; your pinned route should now be serving from x3b-stable-202801 (expected within 5m).
- Ops is collecting diagnostics (KV cache and kernel histograms) — attaching initial snapshot.
- We’ll keep you updated every hour and provide a full postmortem by EOD 29 Feb.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this affects your SLA. I’ll follow up with a summary of root cause and next steps.

— Hannah
Sr. Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: diag_snapshot_20280227.tar.gz (attachment)
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@kensington-analytics.com>, support@kensington-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 27 Feb 2028 11:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 5xx spike from model-x3b affecting inference jobs

Quick internal update and note for the customer thread (cc’ing for visibility).

Summary of findings so far:
- Trigger: a new kernel selection heuristic landed in canary on 2028-02-25 that aggressively switches to a lower-latency NVLink path for long seq lengths. Under sustained small-token, high-concurrency workloads the heuristic thrashes KV cache alignment which led to cache misses and serialization stalls in the attention path. That manifests as elevated 5xx (502/503) and some 504s at the serving layer.
- Scope: only model-x3b (v1) in us-west-2; other models/regions unaffected.
- Mitigation applied: traffic rerouted to x3b-stable-202801 + canary rollback scheduled. We also pushed a temporary fallback that pins kernel selection for affected customers.

Next steps (internal):
1) Complete rollback and run controlled ingress tests (Ops).
2) Patch heuristic to include concurrency threshold; will include small unit tests to prevent cache thrash.
3) Postmortem doc + regression tests to be published.

I’ll prepare a customer-facing postmortem draft for Hannah to review. Ben, please attach the patch diff for the fallback policy.

— Olga
Principal Applied ML Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: x3b-fallback-policy-diff.patch (attachment)
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@kensington-analytics.com>, support@kensington-analytics.com
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 29 Feb 2028 15:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Availability disruption for model-x3b: customer briefing & postmortem follow-up

Hi Marta — follow-up with the post-incident summary and next steps. Thank you for your patience.

What happened (high level):
- On 2028-02-25 we shipped a kernel-selection heuristic to canary that attempted to optimize NVLink paths for long sequences. Under the small-token + high-concurrency pattern typical of your batch scoring, the heuristic caused KV-cache misalignment and increased contention, which led to a rise in 502/503/504 responses from the serving runtime for model-x3b (v1) in us-west-2.

Impact:
- For KD-9412 we observed a 6x increase in 5xx rate for x3b-v1 during the window 08:40–10:20 PST on 2028-02-27. Several scheduled batch jobs experienced retries and extended completion times; no data was lost.

Mitigation and customer-facing actions taken: 
- Traffic for KD-9412 was routed to x3b-stable-202801 within ~5 minutes of detection.
- Canary rollback completed 2028-02-27 12:05 PST.
- We applied a temporary kernel-selection pin for accounts that match the small-token, high-concurrency pattern.

Root cause and fix: 
- Root cause: an aggressive canary change to kernel selection that lacks a concurrency-aware safeguard.
- Permanent fix: we implemented a concurrency-threshold in the heuristic and added regression tests to prevent KV-cache thrash in future releases. Expected rollout to canary 2028-03-05 and to stable 2028-03-12 after validation.

Compensation and next steps:
- We will credit KD-9412 for API error-time during the incident window; Ben will follow up with a formal credit proposal.
- We have scheduled a 1:1 technical review (30m) to walk through the postmortem details and confirm your routing config. Proposed slots: Mon 2028-03-05 10:00-10:30 PST or Tue 2028-03-06 14:00-14:30 PST — please let us know which works.

Attached is the internal postmortem PDF and the diagnostic snapshot we collected. If you want a deeper dive on the kernel heuristics we can have Olga join the call.

Thanks again for raising this quickly — we aim to avoid regressions like this and appreciate the partnership.

Warmly,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference
